system.name: vCXLGen
system.one_liner: the first system that automatically synthesizes and formally verifies CXL bridges reconciling different host cache-coherence protocols and memory models

components.name: CXL Memory Expander Node
components.role: shared memory device implementing the CXL global protocol

components.name: Memory Controller
components.role: controls the CXL memory expander's backing memory

components.name: Intel Compute Node
components.role: a host running the Intel local coherence protocol

components.name: ARM Compute Node
components.role: a host running the Arm local coherence protocol

components.name: Global CC
components.role: host-side cache controller that emits global-protocol requests when local operations can't be satisfied locally; mirrored in the ARM Compute Node

components.name: LLC
components.role: the host's last-level cache; mirrored in the ARM Compute Node

components.name: Local Directory
components.role: tracks local-protocol coherence state for the host's private caches; mirrored in the ARM Compute Node

components.name: Private Cache
components.role: a core's private cache; mirrored in the ARM Compute Node

components.name: CXL Bridges
components.role: translates and propagates local- and global-protocol requests between each host's coherence domain and the shared CXL directory

content.key_idea: Two heterogeneous hosts keep their own local coherence protocol internally, while CXL bridges translate their local requests into nested global CXL.mem transactions against a shared directory.
content.reading_order: Bottom-up: private caches and local directories at the bottom, up through the CXL bridges to the shared Global Directory on top.

summary: Figure 3 shows the CXL bridge operating principle on a concrete two-host example: an Intel Compute Node running the Intel local protocol and an ARM Compute Node running the Arm protocol both attach to a shared CXL Memory Expander Node, whose Global Directory and Memory Controller implement the CXL global protocol. Inside each compute node, private caches issue local requests to a Local Directory, which a bridge (drawn as a dashed CXL Bridges band spanning both Global CC/LLC blocks) translates into CXL requests and forwards to the Global Directory; the ten numbered arrows (ld/st, Intel/Arm request-response pairs, CXL request/forward/response, and a writeback to the Memory Controller) trace one such nested round trip. A three-colour legend marks which parts of the drawing belong to the Intel protocol, the Arm protocol, or the shared CXL protocol.
summary_zh: 该图以英特尔与ARM两台主机共享CXL内存扩展节点为例，展示CXL桥的工作原理：本地请求经本地目录由桥转换为CXL请求并转发至全局目录，十个编号箭头描绘一次嵌套往返。
notes: layout-proposal: bridge-between-domains — two heterogeneous host coherence domains (Intel and Arm, each with their own local protocol) connect through CXL Bridge components to a shared CXL directory/memory controller; host-device captures the host/device split but not the bridge-translation role drawn between them.
